subject: science
passage: In 1912, the German scientist Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined and had slowly drifted apart. He pointed to the way the coasts of South America and Africa seem to fit together and to matching fossils found on both sides of the Atlantic. Most geologists rejected the idea, largely because Wegener could not explain what force could move entire continents. Only in the 1960s, after studies of the ocean floor showed that new crust forms along mid-ocean ridges and spreads outward, did his central idea win wide acceptance.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes a scientific debate and explains why that debate has never been fully settled.
choices.B: It presents an idea, explains its early rejection, and describes its later acceptance.
choices.C: It compares the fossils of South America with those of Africa in detail.
choices.D: It explains how studies of the ocean floor led geologists to reject a theory.

explanation.why: The text introduces Wegener's proposal and his evidence, then says most geologists "rejected the idea" because he had no mechanism. The last sentence explains that ocean-floor studies in the 1960s led the idea to "win wide acceptance." The text moves from proposal, to rejection, to acceptance.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The last sentence says Wegener's idea won wide acceptance, so the debate was largely settled.
explanation.B: Correct. The text presents continental drift, gives the reason it was first rejected, and explains how later evidence led to its acceptance.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The matching fossils are mentioned briefly as Wegener's evidence; they are not compared in detail.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The ocean-floor studies supported Wegener's idea; they did not lead geologists to reject it.
